title: Economics of machine intelligence: texts from 1952 to 2026 that state, contest or bear on its propositions
question: Which located texts, from 1952 to 2026, state, contest or bear on propositions about the economics of machine intelligence? Three strands are recorded. The first is the debate over whether machine intelligence could make economic growth explosive. The second is how mainstream economics treated automation, computers and AI. The third is how economists took up recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI, ideas mostly discussed outside economics. For each proposition, which text by an economist is the earliest located, and which text outside that group?

title: Machine succession, scale and acceleration: propositions in located texts, 1863–2026
question: Which located texts, from 1863 to 2026, state, contest or bear on ten propositions about machine intelligence: that machines succeed humans, that this would be acceptable, that minds move into machines, that building such machines brings conflict, that machine intelligence vastly exceeds human intelligence, that capital is itself a machine intelligence, that intelligence is its own end, that development should be accelerated, and that machine intelligence is a cosmic process that spreads beyond Earth? For each proposition, which text is the earliest located?
